prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and active sites

statement.case_for: I keep B041 first after reading the openings. Zeolite and molecular-sieve catalyst design is a complete chemical story: organic structure-directing agents and new framework topologies (Zones, Davis), and active-site engineering and multifunctional catalysis (Corma), turned into catalytic cracking, selective reduction of NOx and shape-selective fine-chemical processes at very large scale. The structure-to-function link has been verified with diffraction and microscopy, not just asserted, and decades of independent confirmation mean there is no maturity concern. The three names map onto three distinct, defensible contributions: design principle, synthesis, and active-site control and application.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that B041 is a broad, accumulated field rather than a single discovery. Foundational zeolite science predates this list (Barrer, Breck and others), Yu and Tsapatsis have real claims, and a three-person cut is therefore not unique. It also earned only one first-place ranking, so it is a minority view in this committee. My proximity to porous-materials structure determination probably inflates my sense of how well its attribution can be defended. B017 has far broader support and cleaner evidence of impact.

responses.point: B017 sequencing-by-synthesis is chemistry that enabled nearly all modern biomedicine, with the Cambridge pair as the coherent core and a two-person prize the cleanest.
responses.response: I accept the impact and the maturity: it is overdue, and I rank it as my first alternative. My reservation is attribution. Aili and Chabes propose two names, Aqvist and Linke add Mayer, and Ju and Rothberg are credited on the shortlist. The claim to the Solexa chemistry rests on reversible terminators and cluster amplification, and I would want the committee to say explicitly why Ju's terminator chemistry and Rothberg's distinct pyrosequencing route fall outside the citation. If it can, I could support Balasubramanian and Klenerman. I do not think impact alone should decide it over B041, where the structure-function evidence is equally direct.

responses.point: Nitrogenase (B003) unites genetics, crystallography, spectroscopy and kinetics into a physical-chemical account of multi-electron catalysis, with a mature structural record since 1992.
responses.response: As a structural chemist I value the crystallography, and the FeMo-cofactor and its central carbide are a real achievement. But Brzezinski himself notes that the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site are still debated, and Chabes also calls it partly early. A Nobel citation would have to say what the prize recognizes: the structure, which is settled, or the mechanism, which is not. With five credited names split across structure, genetics and kinetics, I find B003 a harder three-person cut than B041. I am glad to be corrected if he thinks the carbide and E4 state work settles the mechanism.

responses.point: Halide perovskites (B045) offer a clear physical principle and a large generative potential, with efficiencies independently reproduced and tandem commercialisation under way.
responses.response: I rank B045 second myself and agree on the principle and the reproducibility. Linke concedes that long-term stability is unresolved, and I would put more weight on that, together with lead toxicity, because it leaves the practical impact unproven in the way zeolite catalysis is proven. Attribution is also crowded among six names, and Kojima is off the list. I would not oppose B045 and think it is a stronger candidate than the biology-adjacent options, but I would not put it ahead of B041 yet.

responses.point: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B048) is the clearest method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, with Buchwald and Hartwig as a clean two-person prize complementary to 2010.
responses.response: I agree that the maturity and attribution are the cleanest on the shortlist, and I ranked B048 third. My qualification is originality relative to the 2010 prize: the committee would have to argue it is a distinct achievement rather than an extension of Pd cross-coupling. Somfai thinks it is complementary, and as a synthetic specialist his view carries weight on that point. I would support it as a strong alternative, but not as the first choice over a materials-and-catalysis achievement that has no recent prize in the same area.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards B041 as one discovery or an accumulation of incremental advances, and whether Yu or Tsapatsis should displace one of the three names.
Whether the claims of Ju and Rothberg in B017 are strong enough that a two- or three-person Cambridge-centred prize is not defensible.
How much weight maturity of the mechanism should receive for B003 and of clinical benefit for B052, compared with the established impact of B041.
statement.conflict_note: My research field (electron crystallography of zeolites, MOFs and porous materials, with Stockholm's MOF and zeolite programme) is very close to B041 and also to B060 and B018. This is a field-proximity disclosure rather than a personal connection to any named candidate: nothing in my profile indicates a collaboration or institutional tie with Corma, Davis or Zones. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, whose first choice is B003, which is not a recusal issue.
